Yeah me neither.

Turns all players into furry/anthro characters. There are currently 5 species:
- Border Collie
- Red Fox
- Arctic Fox

- Whitetail Deer

Like with my last mods, I haven't tested on the latest version. Should work in multiplayer, at least it worked for me. Also seems to work in singleplayer I think.

data.name: ForestTalk
data.shortDescription: Actually talk to Kelvin and Virginia. Kelvin, now deaf, still has plenty to say. Chat through his notepad or hit O for a quick shortcut. Give him real in-game orders. Deep customization included.
data.description:
ForestTalk turns Kelvin and Virginia into real companions, not silent bots you just watch.

💬 How to talk to them
With Kelvin, open his notepad and press T to type. You can also press O while nearby and looking at him, no notepad needed. Virginia works the same way: get close, look at her, and press O, if she's willing.

🧠 Kelvin, your companion
I put a lot of effort into making him aware of his surroundings: nearby danger, your state, the weather, what he's doing. This mod assumes the crash left him deaf, but he can still speak. He's not a bot you click through, he's your companion, and he'll always have something to say. Warm personality, a bit shaken by what he's been through, with a strong moral compass against the forest.

You can also give him real orders through chat: bring logs, repair the camp, build a fire, stay put, follow you, and more. Real orders he carries out in-game.

🌿 Virginia, an independent soul
Virginia can talk with you too, on her own terms: a fully independent person. She can't be given orders or commands, she'll only chat if she feels like it.

⚠️ Real environmental awareness
Both react to what's actually happening: danger, injuries, hunger or thirst, night, rain. I dug deep into the game's code so this isn't a chat bolted on top, they react to what's going on with you.

👀 Bonus: let them see what you see
Type !look plus your message (e.g. !look what do you think of our base?) to send a screenshot along with it. A fun little extra, not required. Heads up: capturing it pauses the game for a split second.

⚙️ Deep customization
Choose between several AI providers: Player2 (a button to generate your API key instantly), OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, or your own custom/local server. Adjust how often they speak on their own, toggle danger comments, write custom personality notes, and more.

Surviving the forest is no longer something you do alone. Kelvin and Virginia become real friends to face the island with.

data.name: Character Select
data.shortDescription: Choose your player appearance and keep it across sessions. Works in multiplayer.
data.description:
Sons of the Forest gives you a random appearance every time you join a server, and there is no way to choose. This mod lets you pick the one you want and automatically reapplies it every time your player spawns, so you stay the same character.

Press F9 in game to cycle through the eight appearances. The current one is shown on screen as you cycle. Your choice is saved and applied automatically on every spawn.

If your keyboard has no F keys, or you would rather pick one directly, press F1 to open the console and use the CHARACTER command.

Client side only. Nothing needs to be installed on a dedicated server. Your appearance replicates through normal game networking, so other players see your choice even if they do not have the mod installed.

Source: https://github.com/JustinOros/sotf-character-select

data.name: Freshwater is Drinkable
data.shortDescription: Running water is safe (except when contaminated). Stagnant water is not.
data.description:
REQUIRES https://sotf-mods.com/mods/brutechiefton/uicoordinator


What to expect
--
Filling a flask or pot from a clean source will give you clean water. Drinking from a clean source will not make you sick, it will actually clear some sickness (just like clean/boiled water).

Doing the same at a dirty water source will still give you dirty water and make you sick as normal.

*Note: Only the water sources on the surface have been mapped. 


The mod works by querying against the water graph to find the nearest node. An unmapped water source will therefore use the nearest one, which may or may not not make sense. 


If this bothers you, please use the in-game editor (F7, add last target) to add a node and program it as desired.


Caves and their water sources are currently unmapped.*


Details
--
The mod comes with a water graph that I drew by hand. I marked all the rivers and streams as clean, and every stagnant pool/pond as dirty. 

Each new save's water graph will be loaded from this canonical graph. You can see and edit the water graph by pressing F7. 

Changes made will be saved when you save your game. Different saves can have different graphs.

To overwrite the default water graph, press export. 
To reload the default, press reload.

Dedicated server graphs cannot be edited at this time.

data.name: UICoordinator
data.shortDescription: Enable cursor when any menu is open. Disable when they're all closed.
data.description:
UICoordinator provides reference-counted ownership of menu input. While one or more mod menus hold a lease, UICoordinator unlocks and displays the cursor, places the game input system into menu mode, and suppresses mouse-look. When the final menu releases its lease, the previous cursor and input state are restored.

This prevents independent mod menus from fighting over the cursor or restoring gameplay input while another menu remains open.

Download and check out the readme if you'd like to use it for your own mods.

data.name: Chronos
data.shortDescription: Set day length in real minutes and season length in in-game days, per save, while you play.
data.description:
Day length as a count of real minutes, season length as a count of in-game days, changed at any time in a loaded save. The game gives you four presets, picked at world setup before you know how that world plays, and changing your mind later means editing the save.

**Day length.** The vanilla presets in real time: Short 29.4 minutes, Default 58.7, Long 2h 58m, Realistic 24h. Custom takes anything from 0.1 to 10080 minutes. The panel splits the result into daylight and night. Night runs 2.7 times faster, so a 60-minute day gives you 41 minutes of light.

**Season length.** Presets in in-game days per season: 3, 5, 10, 91. Custom takes 1 to 120 whole days, since a season turns over at midnight. The season is worked out from the current day, so switching the calendar re-reads the year you already played.

**Snow keeps pace.** Snow is a height line that winter walks down the mountains at a fixed rate. On short days a season can end before the line has finished moving. Chronos scales that rate with your day length.

**Usage.** Load a save, open Options, then Mods, then Chronos. Turn on the day override, the season override or both, pick a preset or type your own number, close the panel. Values live inside the save and travel with it.

**Multiplayer.** Works in co-op. Every player needs the mod and the same numbers. The clock comes from the host, but hunger, thirst and the season turn over on each player's own day length. Dedicated servers are untested.

**Compatibility.** Chronos writes the clock speed (TimeOfDayHolder.GetBaseSpeedMultiplier), the season durations (SeasonsManager.GetSeasonDurations) and eight transition fields on SnowHeightManager. Another mod that writes any of them will fight it, and the one that applied last wins.

**Install.** Install RedLoader and run the game once, then unpack the archive into the game folder. You should end up with Mods/Chronos.dll and Mods/Chronos/manifest.json.

Source: github.com/Cyace84/sotf-chronos (MIT)

data.name: SnapPointSelectorMod
data.shortDescription: A mod that allows cycle through available snap points when placing log/rock/stick.
data.description:
Simple Mod for Sons of the Forest that allows to choose which snap-point log/rock/stick should snap to.

Usage:

Hold Left Alt and scroll the mouse wheel to cycle through the available snap points for the object you're placing.

Notes:

- The mod only cycles through snap points that the game has generated for your current position and viewing angle.
- Depending on where you're standing and what you're looking at, some snap points may not be available until you move or change your camera angle.
- As a result, you may sometimes see only a subset of the possible snap points.

data.name: Mason Line
data.shortDescription: Build from here to there. Two stakes, a cord between them, and every log you set down snaps to it.
data.description:
A craftable guide line for straight walls. The game stacks logs perfectly, but the angle comes from the first log, dropped by hand with nothing to line up against, and it cannot be nudged afterwards. Mason Line supplies it: plant a stake where the wall starts and another where it ends, a cord pulls tight between them, and anything you set down beside the cord snaps onto it.

Crafted from 2 sticks and 1 rope on the crafting mat.

**Controls.** No custom keybinds. Left-click plants a stake, first A then B. Hold Dismantle (C by default) on a stake to collect the line and get the bundle back.

**What snaps.** Logs flat or standing, standing sticks, campfires, rocks. Anything you set down loose on open ground. Guidebook blueprints, the ghosts you fill in piece by piece, do not.

**Multiple lines.** Each bundle is one line and they all work at once; a log goes to the closest cord. Aim a new line's first stake at a standing one and it lands exactly on it, so a run can turn a corner. Squaring the angle between two lines is still your job.

**Settings.** Snap distance, reach past the stakes and stake magnet, in the mod menu.

**Co-op.** Works in a peer-to-peer game. Lines are private: you see your own stakes, and only your own placements snap to them. The logs themselves are placed by the game as usual, so everyone sees the same wall. Dedicated servers are untested.

**Limitations.** Lines are not part of the save: reload and the line is gone, its bundle back in your pack. The cord is a guide, not an object, so everything walks through it.

**Mod conflicts.** The bundle takes item id 9417. If another mod already owns it, Mason Line refuses to register rather than overwrite, and says so in the log; `UserData/MasonLine.cfg` can point it elsewhere. 
Bug reports: attach `_Redloader/Latest.log`. 
Thanks to ToniMacaroni for RedLoader and SonsSdk.

Full description and source: [GitHub](https://github.com/Cyace84/sotf-mason-line) (MIT)

data.name: AutoRemoveDead
data.shortDescription: Simple mod that automatically executes the console command removedead seamlessly, so you don't have to type it every time.
data.description:
Simple mod that automatically executes the console command removedead seamlessly, so you don't have to type it every time.

Works well with zombie horde-style bases and mods like AttractShrineCustomizer.

The goal is to prevent your FPS from dropping due to having too many dead bodies around.

Features:

Adjustable interval from 0 to 600 seconds in the config file or in-game.
Tested and confirmed to work as the Host.

Enjoy.
